To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interaction between Arap3, a PI3K effactor, and SHIP2, a negative regulator of the PI3K signaling pathway, is mediated by the SAM domains of both proteins.
Arap3 interacts with SHIP2 in the plasma membrane and that the interaction is dependent on the SAM domain of both proteins.
Arap3 interacts with SHIP2 via the SAM domain of both proteins and that the interaction is mediated in vitro by a heterodimer of SAM domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel interaction partners of Arap proteins.
the identification of new interaction partners for Arap3 and with the characterization of the interaction of Arap3 with the PI(4,5) phosphatase SH2IP.
the identification and characterization of novel interaction partners of Arap 3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction between the two proteins is mediated by their SAM domains and that this interaction can be used to regulate SHIP2 activity in a spatially and temporally regulated manner.
the interaction of Arap3 and its effector SHIP2 is mediated by the SAM domains of both proteins.
the SAM domain in Arap3 is involved in the recruitment of SHIP2 into the PI(3)P3 effector complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SAM domain can be used to recruit a negative effector of PI3K into the PI3K effactor complex to regulate PI3K signaling.
the SAM domain is involved in the recruitment of SHIP2 to the plasma membrane.
Arap3 can interact with both a positive regulator of PI3 kinase signaling and a negative regulator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SAM domains have a function in protein-protein interactions, which is different from their function in protein-proteins interactions.
Arap3 can function as a scaffold for a PI3K effactor complex.
SAM domains are not only used to mediate homo- and heterodimerization of proteins, but also to mediate interactions between different proteins in a hetero-dimeric fashion.
